pages.text: Glassworking turns sand into glass. First make a $(thing)Glass Batch$(). The colour of the sand decides which kind it is:$(br)$(br)$(li)Black sand: $(thing)Volcanic$()$(li)Green or brown sand: $(thing)Olivine$()$(li)Yellow, red or pink sand: $(thing)Hematitic$()$(li)White sand: $(thing)Silica$()
A batch is crafted from sand of one of those colours, $(l:crafting/glassworking#lime)Lime$() and a $(l:crafting/glassworking#potash)Potash$().
$(thing)Lime$() is one of the parts of a batch. It is a powder got by $(l:core_mechanics/heating)heating$() $(l:metalworking/flux)Flux$() to 840 °C. Borax flux does not burn to lime.

A $(thing)Potash$() or its like is the other part. $(thing)Soda Ash$() will do, a powder got by firing $(thing)Dried Seaweed$() or $(thing)Kelp$(), and so will $(l:the_world/ores_and_minerals#saltpeter)Saltpeter$().

Glass is worked from a batch through a series of steps, and some steps need a tool:$(li)$(thing)Saw$(): a $(l:crafting/glassworking#saw)Gem Saw$()$(li)$(thing)Pinch$(): $(l:crafting/glassworking#jacks)Jacks$()$(li)$(thing)Flatten$(): a $(l:crafting/glassworking#paddle)Paddle$()$(li)$(thing)Blow$() and $(thing)Stretch$(): a $(l:crafting/glassworking#blowpipe)Blowpipe$()
pages.title: Tools of the Trade

pages.text: The key tool is the $(thing)Blowpipe$(). Knap it from clay and fire it into a $(thing)Ceramic Blowpipe$().
Ceramic blowpipes are brittle and may break in use. A sturdier pipe is forged at the anvil from a $(thing)Brass Rod$(), but brass melts at 930 °C.
$(thing)Flatten$() is done with a $(thing)Paddle$(), made of wood.
$(thing)Pinch$() is done with $(thing)Jacks$(), two brass rods welded together.
$(thing)Saw$() is done with a $(thing)Gem Saw$(), which also breaks $(thing)Glass Blocks$() and $(thing)Glass Panes$() so that you can take them.

Heat the glass on the pipe to $(4)$(bold)Faint Red$() first. For each step, hold the blowpipe and keep $(item)$(k:key.use)$() pressed.$(br2)$(bold)Blow$(): use the pipe looking straight ahead.$(br)$(bold)Stretch$(): use it looking straight down.
pages.title: How to Glass

pages.text: $(bold)Flatten$(): use the pipe with a $(l:crafting/glassworking#paddle)Paddle$() in the off hand.$(br)$(bold)Pinch$(): with $(l:crafting/glassworking#jacks)Jacks$() in the off hand.$(br)$(bold)Saw$(): with a $(l:crafting/glassworking#saw)Gem Saw$() in the off hand.$(br)$(bold)Roll$(): with a $(l:crafting/weaving#wool_cloth)Wool Cloth$() in the off hand.

Glass is worked while the pipe is hot, and not hotter than the pipe stands. Ordinary glass works from $(4)Faint Red$() (480 °C). $(thing)Borosilicate$() glass, made of sand and borax with no lime, needs 1250 °C. Brass melts at 930 °C, so only a ceramic pipe will do for it, between 1250 and 1500 °C: above that TFC returns the pipe empty. See $(l:tfcpp/glass)Borosilicate Glass$().
